sources.title: AFI Catalog: The Exorcist (1973)
supports: Ellen Burstyn is credited as Chris MacNeil; William Friedkin directed; William Peter Blatty wrote and produced from his own novel.
The production cooled Regan’s room below freezing to make actors’ breath visible.
AFI records live-source sound-effects recording and distinguishes the 2000 DVD director’s cut from the original theatrical release.
sources.limits: The possession narrative is fiction and does not establish medical, psychiatric, or religious facts. This report excludes AFI’s Linda Blair ‘film debut’ and Max von Sydow age claims pending independent verification.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 46th Academy Awards (1974)
supports: The Exorcist received ten nominations and two wins.
It won Sound for Robert Knudson and Chris Newman and Adapted Screenplay for William Peter Blatty.
Ellen Burstyn, Linda Blair, and Jason Miller appear as acting nominees for the film.
sources.limits: The awards ledger supports categories and outcomes, not the fiction’s supernatural, medical, or religious propositions.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: Network (1976)
supports: Peter Finch is credited as Howard Beale; Sidney Lumet directed and Paddy Chayefsky wrote.
AFI records the promotion of the ‘I’m as mad as hell’ slogan.
AFI documents the subsequent CBS television-rights acquisition and edits for broadcast.
sources.limits: Howard Beale and the television company are fictional. The promotional slogan and later broadcast edits do not establish facts about real journalism or television audiences.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 49th Academy Awards (1977)
supports: Network received ten nominations and four wins.
Peter Finch won Actor in a Leading Role for Network.
Faye Dunaway, Beatrice Straight, and Paddy Chayefsky won in their listed categories; Holden, Beatty, Roizman, Lumet, and Heim received the additional nominations.
sources.limits: This awards ledger supports categories and outcomes only; it does not make the fictional television narrative documentary evidence.
